title: indigo_agent_scheduler: score the altitude relative to the target's culmination, tasks ran at dusk instead of near their transit
description:
Owner observation: with several tasks the scheduler runs them all from the beginning of the night instead of close to their culmination.

Cause: the altitude score term is absolute (`altitude = 100 * altitude / 90` at the current time, SCHEDULER.md "Selection"). It does not tell a rising target from one at transit, and a high-declination target always outranks a southern one even at that one's best time. Other dispatch schedulers (ACP Scheduler efficiency index, Liverpool/ANU 2.3 m/Palomar 60" merit functions) rank by how close a target is to its own best position (hour angle or airmass relative to transit), which spreads runs around each target's culmination.

Change: the altitude term becomes relative to the target's own upper culmination:
  altitude = 100 * max(0, alt_now) / alt_transit, where alt_transit = 90 - |latitude - declination| (the target's altitude at upper culmination; use the same coordinates/epoch handling as the existing altitude computation)
- 0 without `@target`, as today; clamp to 0..100.
- ALTITUDE_WEIGHT keeps its name, range and default and now weights the relative term.
- The night plan simulation uses the same score, so the plan shows the new order.
- No new waiting behaviour: the scheduler still never idles while a task is eligible (a lone task still starts at dusk; `@ha` remains the per-task hard window).

Tests: unit tests for the score term (target at transit = 100, half its transit altitude = 50, below horizon = 0, no target = 0, a southern target at transit outranks a higher northern target far from transit) and plan/selection tests showing two targets with different transit times each run near its own transit instead of both at dusk. Update existing tests that assumed the absolute term.
Docs: SCHEDULER.md (Selection, settings table ALTITUDE_WEIGHT, survey if relevant), INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md (score explanation, ALTITUDE_WEIGHT), PROPERTIES.md (AGENT_SCHEDULER_SETTINGS ALTITUDE_WEIGHT description). Bump DRIVER_VERSION.

outcome.summary: Pass. Astronomy: alt_transit = 90 - |lat - dec| equals asin(cos(lat - dec)), the HA=0 altitude, for every lat/dec incl. southern, circumpolar (upper culmination) and never-rising (<=0 -> term 0); computed from the JNow dec right after indigo_j2k_to_jnow in indigo_scheduler_target_build (sky.c:140), same coords as the geometric (no refraction) altitude grid; relative term clamped to 100 and alt<=0 gives 0 (plan.c:41-44). Selection (scheduler.c:1549) and plan (plan.c:140) both call indigo_scheduler_score. transit_altitude is set in target_build together with altitude[], so it is rebuilt by every existing path (task change build_target, site/grid rebuild at scheduler.c:1532-1539). Docs consistent across SCHEDULER.md, guide and PROPERTIES.md; DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000018 -> 0x03000019; git diff --check clean. Tests: altitude_term covers transit=100, half=50, below horizon=0, no target=0, never rises; altitude_term_is_relative covers south-at-transit vs higher north; runs_near_transit uses a fixed UTC timestamp, fixed site and sky.lst-derived RAs (no local time), and would fail under the old absolute term (late dec 70 target is ~32.6 deg vs ~30.4 deg at dusk, so it would run first). Minor, non-blocking: the integration case sky_bonuses_order_equal_priorities (test_agent_scheduler.c:2827) uses two dec-0 targets at latitude 0, equal transit altitudes, so it does not exercise the relative behaviour the SCHEDULER.md survey line now names (unit tests do); no reproduction note recorded in the ticket per the bugfixes rule. Ran: test_agent_scheduler_plan 19/19 PASS, test_agent_scheduler 81/81 PASS.

history.text: Building and running scheduler unit tests

Reproduction: unit test runs_near_transit (indigo_test/unit/test_agent_scheduler_plan.c) fails on the old absolute altitude term - at dusk the dec 70 target (32.6 deg) outranks the early-transit target (30.4 deg) and runs first; altitude_term and altitude_term_is_relative also fail on the old code. All pass after the change. Coordinator rerun of the full test_agent_scheduler suite: 125 run, 125 passed.

checks.name: unit
checks.command: make Makefile.inc && make init && make -j8 -C indigo_libs all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_platesolver -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/system_alpaca -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -C indigo_test test-unit
